title: The 50/30/20 Rule Says Save $899 a Month. Could You? #shorts
description:
The 50/30/20 rule on a typical paycheck: the typical full-time worker takes home about $4,496 a month after federal taxes (BLS median weekly earnings Q3 2026, $1,239 x 52 = $64,428 a year, minus 2026 federal income tax for a single filer and FICA; state tax not included). 50% to needs: $2,248. 30% to wants: $1,349. 20% to savings or extra debt payments: $899. At an example 7% a year, $899 a month for 10 years grows to about $155,600 (you put in $107,880). 7% is an illustration, not a promise: real returns vary and can be negative; taxes, fees and inflation are not included.

The 50/30/20 rule was popularized by Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi in the 2005 book All Your Worth.

This video is for education only and is not financial advice.
